name: Airlift Challenge
description: Airlift operations require the timely distribution of various cargo, much of which is time sensitive and valuable. However, these operations have to contend with sudden disruptions from weather and malfunctions, requiring immediate rescheduling. The Airlift Challenge competition seeks possible solutions via a simulator that provides a simplified abstraction of the airlift problem. The simulator uses an OpenAI gym interface that allows participants to create an algorithm for planning agent actions. The algorithm is scored using a remote evaluator against scenarios of ever-increasing difficulty. The second iteration of the competition was underway from November 2023 to April 2024. In this paper, we describe the competition and simulation environment. As a step towards applying generalized planning techniques to the problem, we present a temporal PDDL domain for the Pickup and Delivery Problem, a model which lies at the core of the Airlift Challenge.
reputation: A niche competition benchmark used in the planning and operations research community to evaluate robust scheduling and rescheduling approaches under disruptions.
notes: Competition- and simulator-specific evaluation — risk of overfitting to the simulator; scenarios vary in difficulty and stochasticity; not a large-scale standardized dataset; leaderboard-driven comparisons.
